# Injection well volumes, one regulator workbook a year (form 1012A layout)

`uic_workbook` · adapter 1.0.0 · makes `fluid_injection` tokens

| | |
|---|---|
| Provider | The regulator the region names (Oklahoma Corporation Commission) |
| Home | https://oklahoma.gov/occ/divisions/oil-gas/oil-gas-data.html |
| Licence | `LicenseRef-per-region` |

## Terms

Oklahoma's UIC volumes are public records of the Oklahoma Corporation Commission, published for download with no licence attached; cite the Commission and the year's file.

## Cite

- Oklahoma Corporation Commission, Oil and Gas Conservation Division: UIC Injection Volumes by Year (form 1012A), https://oklahoma.gov/occ/divisions/oil-gas/oil-gas-data.html

## Access

One .xlsx workbook per year from the URL pattern the region gives, downloaded once and cached by hash; read with the standard library (`craton.adapters.xlsx`).

## From the source to the token

| Token slot | Comes from |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `forcing` |
| `lat, lon` | the well's surface location |
| `depth_km` | middle of the injection interval (feet → km), else total depth |
| `time` | first day of the month, 00:00 UTC; resolution one month |
| `value` | the month's volume, in m³ (barrels × 0.158987) |
| `qualifiers` | well ← API number, well_class, fluid, formation |

## Uncertainty

Assumed: 5% of the volume when metered, 20% when calculated, 30% otherwise.

## Known issues

- Before 2011 the layout differs (one .xls for 2006-2010); not read.
- The newest years are revised weekly, so the cached bytes are one version of them; the raw store keeps which.
- Reports are yearly: a forecast that reads last month's volume assumes it is known by then, which only the weekly Arbuckle reports (since 2016) make true.
- Wells of every class are kept; enhanced-recovery wells inject about as much as disposal wells but rarely shake anything, so readers choose by well_class.
